record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: If X is an algebraic extension of the rationals, what is the chromatic number of the two-dimensional space X^2 under the usual Euclidean unit-distance coloring rule?

evidence.quote: The authors pose some problems in their conclusion: try to determine χ(Qn ) for some n ≥ 5 (in [4], K. B. Chilakamarri shows that χ(Q5 ) ≥ 6), or try to find χ(X 2 ) where X is some algebraic extension of Q, perhaps Q[ 2].

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X \subseteq \overline{\mathbb{Q}} \cap \mathbb{R}$ be an algebraic extension of the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$ (for instance $X = \mathbb{Q}[\sqrt{2}]$). Consider the unit-distance graph $G(X^2)$ whose vertex set is $X^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and in which two points $p, q \in X^2$ are joined by an edge if and only if their Euclidean distance equals $1$, that is, $\|p-q\|_2 = 1$. Determine the chromatic number $\chi(G(X^2))$, i.e., the least cardinal $k$ for which there exists a map $c \colon X^2 \to \{1,2,\dots,k\}$ such that $c(p) \neq c(q)$ whenever $\|p-q\|_2 = 1$.
artifact.category_tag: Euclidean Ramsey theory / chromatic number of the plane
artifact.status_search_result: No published determination of the chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on $X^2$ for algebraic extensions $X$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ (e.g., $\mathbb{Q}[\sqrt{2}]$) was found. Related work establishes lower bounds for unit-distance graphs over $\mathbb{Q}^n$ and locates 5-chromatic finite unit-distance graphs with coordinates in algebraic extensions like $\mathbb{Q}[\sqrt{3},\sqrt{5},\sqrt{11}]$, but the precise value of $\chi(X^2)$ for general algebraic extensions remains undetermined. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Coordinates of the smallest known 5-chromatic unit distance graph lie in Q[√3, √5, √11].
status_evidence.claim: Specific algebraic extensions arise in known partial results, but no full determination of χ(X^2) for algebraic X is reported.

status_evidence.title: Hadwiger-Nelson problem - Polymath Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of unit distance graphs over Q^n and algebraic subfields without resolution of χ(X^2) for algebraic extensions of Q.
status_evidence.claim: The chromatic number for algebraic extensions of Q in the plane is not reported as resolved.
